title: A longer trip for light
hook: Change distance and predict light-travel time.
misconception: light-travel time stays fixed when distance doubles.
objective: Apply t = d/c to compare light-travel time when distance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With light in vacuum over a fixed inertial frame distance, t = d/c. When distance doubles, light-travel time becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model t = d/c; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider light in vacuum over a fixed inertial frame distance, with a nonzero initial result. If distance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on light-travel time?
recall.why: Apply t = d/c under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
